sections.title: Basic Concept of Ratio
sections.content: A ratio shows the relative size of two or more quantities. Example: Ram:Shyam age ratio = 3:2. If Ram=12 years, Shyam = 12*2/3 = 8 years.

sections.title: Part to Whole Ratio
sections.content: Dividing a total into parts in a given ratio. Example: ₹600 divided in 3:2 → 3 parts=₹360, 2 parts=₹240.

sections.title: Equivalent Ratios
sections.content: Ratios that represent the same relationship. Example: 2:3 = 4:6 = 6:9.

sections.title: Finding the Fourth Term
sections.content: In a proportion, the fourth term can be calculated. Example: 5:8 = ? : 32 → ? = 5*32/8 = 20.

sections.title: Age-Based Problems
sections.content: Use ratios to solve age problems. Example: Father:Son=5:2, Son=12 → Father=12*5/2=30 years.

sections.title: Simple Partnership
sections.content: Profit or investment ratio problems. Example: A invests ₹2000, B invests ₹3000, total profit ₹500 → A’s share = 500*2000/5000=₹200.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Do not add ratios directly to divide.
• Cross-multiply carefully while finding the fourth term.

sections.title: Quick Tips
sections.content:
• Use smaller numbers as base.
• Always cross-multiply for proportions.
• Sum of parts = total.

tricks.title: Quick 100% Calculation
tricks.explanation: 100% of a number = the number itself

tricks.title: Fourth Term Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Cross-multiply to find the unknown term in proportion

tricks.title: Simplify Ratio Quickly
tricks.explanation: Divide both numbers by their GCD
